title: Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan — Where the Tier Review Leaves the Plan
content:
**Rule of the tier review outcome — Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan.**

1. **Ranking.** The tiers rank upward from Paystride Access Starter through Paystride Access Standard, Paystride Access Plus, Paystride Access Preferred and Paystride Access Premier to Paystride Access Premier Plus.

2. **Write-off return.** At a review under the tier review, when the tier carries a write-off reset and the plan's latest write-off was booked on or after its level effective date and on or before the payday reviewed, the plan returns to Paystride Access Starter; otherwise the plan keeps its current tier.

3. **Which review takes a write-off.** A write-off counts at the review of the first payday on or after the day it is booked, a write-off booked on a payday always standing before that payday's review is recorded: one booked after the payday reviewed is taken at the review of the plan's next payday, never at the review recorded for the payday before it, and while such a write-off is the plan's latest the review takes no earlier write-off either, the next payday's review returning the plan to Paystride Access Starter for both. This replaces, for every review under the tier review, the former rule that a write-off returns the plan to Paystride Access Starter at the next level review.

4. **Moving up.** At a review under the tier review the plan moves up one tier when it has no open shortfall and the next tier is within every allowance of this review, and in no other way; this replaces, for every such review, the former rule of moving up on the entry gates of the next tier. At a review of a payday that carries a shortfall no entry gate is tested, as the downgrade prevails. Each allowance names the highest tier it permits; an allowance permits only Paystride Access Starter unless one of its own tiers names a higher tier for the plan, so the next tier is never within an allowance by default; a move up is by one tier and never more.

5. **Open shortfall.** The plan's open shortfall is its outstanding balance less the amount of its transfers carrying its next payday net of the transfer returns carrying that date and less its fees carrying that date net of the fee reversals carrying it, worked to the cent. An open shortfall of zero or less means the plan has none.

## Hypothetical worked cases

*Case A — write-off in the review window.* A plan on Paystride Access Plus has a level effective date of 22 April; the payday reviewed is 2 May; its latest write-off was booked on 29 April. The write-off is on or after 22 April and on or before 2 May, and the tier carries a write-off reset: the plan returns to Paystride Access Starter.

*Case B — write-off booked after the payday.* Same plan, but the latest write-off was booked on 4 May, after the 2 May payday. It is not taken at this review; it is taken at the review of the plan's next payday.

*Case C — open shortfall.* A plan on Paystride Access Standard with no write-off since its level effective date shows an outstanding balance of 212.40 USD; its transfers carrying the next payday total 180.00 USD with no returns, and its fees carrying that date total 4.98 USD with no reversals. The open shortfall is 212.40 less 180.00 less 4.98, 27.42 USD, above zero: the plan does not move up and keeps Paystride Access Standard.

| Write-off booked on or after the level effective date and on or before the payday | Open shortfall | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| yes (write-off reset carried) | any | Paystride Access Starter |
| no | above zero | current tier kept |
